sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill for a house in the City of Homestead?
sections.html:
The Miami-Dade County Office of the Tax Collector sends the bill, because the City of Homestead is a municipality inside Miami-Dade County. The city sets its own rate, as do the county, the School Board and other districts, and the collector only gathers and distributes what they levy.

The collector's main office is at 200 NW 2nd Avenue, Miami, FL 33128, with a customer line at 305-375-5448. The Property Appraiser handles valuation and exemptions, and its homestead line is 305-375-4712. The Clerk of Courts and Comptroller records documents and runs tax deed sales.

Do not confuse the city with the exemption. "Homestead" is both the name of this South Florida city and the Florida tax benefit for a primary residence. A house in the city of Homestead can have a homestead exemption, and plenty of houses elsewhere in Miami-Dade do too.

sections.h2: When do Homestead property tax bills go out, and when are they due?
sections.html:
The collector's page lists October 30, 2026 as the mailing date for 2026 annual notices, and bills may be paid online from that day. Taxes can be paid without penalty through March 31 of the following year.

The discount runs month by month, per the state revenue department and repeated on the county FAQ:

Early payment schedule from the Florida Department of Revenue (floridarevenue.com, Taxpayer information) and the Miami-Dade Tax Collector's real estate page
If paid inDiscount
November4%
December3%
January2%
February1%
MarchGross tax

The collector's FAQ says discounts on mailed checks follow the postmark date. If you pay through your bank's bill-pay service, schedule it at least five business days before the due date and use the folio number from the notice.

sections.h2: What happens if Homestead property tax is not paid?
sections.html:
Unpaid real estate tax turns delinquent on April 1, and Miami-Dade adds at least 3% interest plus advertising costs and fees at that point. Under Florida Statute 197.432, a tax certificate may be issued if 2026 taxes are unpaid before June 1, 2027, and the collector's page says that sale begins June 1, 2027.

The collector warns that a certificate can lead to the loss of the property at a future date. A certificate holder may apply for a tax deed after two years have passed since April 1 of the issue year. The clerk then runs the auction, and the winning bidder posts a deposit of 5 percent of the bid or $200, whichever is greater, with full payment, documentary stamps and recording fees due within 24 hours.

One local wrinkle: if your bill includes a Water, Road and Sewer assessment, such as one collected in 30-year annual installments, the collector says the taxes must be paid by May 31 or a certificate is sold for the remaining balance on that lien. Check your notice for this line item.

sections.h2: What homestead exemption can a Homestead owner claim?
sections.html:
A qualifying owner can claim up to $50,000 off assessed value. The first $25,000 applies to all taxes, and a second $25,000 applies to value over $50,000 for non-school taxes only. The owner must live there as a permanent residence on January 1 and file Form DR-501 with the Property Appraiser by March 1.

  • Renting out the home, moving out, or giving up Florida residency ends the exemption.
  • The state's Save Our Homes cap holds yearly growth in assessed value to the lower of 3 percent or the inflation figure, and the state chart lists 2.7 percent for 2026.
  • A sale, foreclosure or other transfer of title resets the property to just value the following January 1, with exceptions for spouses and some transfers at death.
  • A seller may carry over part of the capped benefit to a new Florida homestead through portability, filed on Form DR-501T with the new application. The new homestead must be established within three years of January 1 of the year the old one was given up.

The county's FAQ points owners to the Property Appraiser for exemption lists and offers an online tax estimator for buyers who want to project a new bill.

sections.h2: How do I question my Homestead property value?
sections.html:
The Property Appraiser mails the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes, called the TRIM notice, each August. A value challenge goes to the Value Adjustment Board through a petition filed within 25 days of the notice date, as the state revenue department describes it.

If an exemption was denied, the petition period is 30 days from the denial letter. File the exemption itself by March 1 so the question never arises.

The county tax collector can also correct refunds that arise from Property Appraiser or board decisions, and its FAQ lists a refund email for that purpose. Taxes affected by a sale are a closing matter between buyer and seller, not a refund from the collector.

sections.h2: What is the City of Homestead millage rate?
sections.html:
The city says its operating millage rate for FY 2026 to 2027 stays the same as the year before, in a budget announcement dated October 2, 2026. That announcement does not print the rate itself, so use your tax notice for the figure.

Two other items are worth a look. The same announcement reports $32 million set aside for capital projects and five new police officer positions. Separately, the city put two general obligation bond questions, one for parks and one for roadways, to voters on November 4, 2025. The city's FAQ estimated about 0.3661 mills for the parks bond and 0.3983 mills for the roadway bond if both passed and were fully issued. Ask the city whether either bond is on your bill, since the FAQ describes borrowing in several series over years.

The collector reminds owners that the total millage on any parcel depends on every district covering it, and that it can be read off the property's tax bill online.

sections.h2: What costs come with selling a house in Homestead?
sections.html:
Miami-Dade County has its own deed stamp rate: the revenue department prints 60 cents per $100 plus a surtax of 45 cents per $100, and the surtax is not due on a document that transfers only a single-family dwelling. Other Florida counties pay 70 cents per $100 statewide. All parties to a document are liable for the tax, regardless of which side agrees to pay it.

Before closing in Homestead:

  • Get a written tax payoff from the collector and ask about any certificate or delinquent notice on the account.
  • Ask the title company how the current year will be prorated, since the collector's FAQ says refunds tied to a sale are resolved at closing.
  • Check the Clerk's records for liens, and confirm whether a Water, Road and Sewer assessment is attached to the parcel.
  • Tell the closing agent whether you used the quarterly installment plan, because a missed first installment by July 31 drops the account from the plan.

If the property has back taxes, an inherited title or repairs a conventional buyer's lender will not accept, a direct cash sale can be closed on a schedule that lets the title company clear the tax from proceeds.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in the City of Homestead?
faqs.a: The Miami-Dade County Office of the Tax Collector, at 200 NW 2nd Avenue in Miami. The city sets its own rate, but it does not send the bill.

faqs.q: When do Homestead taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. The collector adds at least 3% interest, advertising costs and fees to real estate taxes unpaid on that date.

faqs.q: Is a tax certificate the same as losing my house?
faqs.a: No, but it is the first step. A certificate is a lien the collector sells for unpaid tax, and a holder may apply for a tax deed once two years have passed since April 1 of the issue year.

faqs.q: Can I get a lower tax by moving in before January 1?
faqs.a: You must occupy the home as your permanent residence on January 1 and apply by March 1 to claim the exemption for that tax year. A sale also resets the capped value for the buyer the next January 1.

faqs.q: Does the city of Homestead charge its own tax on the sale?
faqs.a: The city's own pages do not list a separate transfer tax, so ask the city clerk to confirm. Florida's deed stamp tax applies, at the Miami-Dade rate printed by the Department of Revenue, and the title company collects it at closing.
